paragraphs: Baker, here's what I see in this passage: God cares about HOW His people come to Him, not just THAT they come. There's a gate that opens on the Sabbath and the New Moon, and the prince bows in worship at the threshold while the people of the land bow at the same entrance (Ezekiel 46:2-3). The prince has his own instructions for where he stands and how his offerings are made (Ezekiel 46:2, 12), but at the appointed feasts he goes in with the people and leaves when they leave (Ezekiel 46:10). Friend, the one with the most still bows, and he doesn't walk in alone.

Then the Lord GOD says the prince must not take any of the inheritance of the people by evicting them, "so that none of My people will be displaced from his property" (Ezekiel 46:18). Worship and how you treat people live in the same passage, and that is NO accident. Whoever has power is told to use it so that God's people have a place to stand. If you can't worship at the gate and then be fair at the fence, I think the worship got stuck at the gate.

And look where the passage ends up: in the kitchens. The priests cook and bake the offerings in their own place "so that they do not bring them into the outer court and transmit holiness to the people" (Ezekiel 46:20), and four matching kitchens with ovens stand ready for those who minister to cook the sacrifices offered by the people (Ezekiel 46:23-24). Baker, God cares about the ordinary, faithful work behind the worship, the daily lamb and the ovens that stay warm. That's why my ovens stay ready too, and your small, steady work in the Word matters more than you know. This vision is not finished yet, so keep your apron on.
